title: Career roadmap · Regulatory Counsel
summary: Build a career combining corporate law, securities regulation, competition law, financial regulation, compliance, enforcement and regulatory policy.

facts.Timeline assumption: Because the starting qualification is already a Ph.D., the normal next step is professional legal/research work, postdoctoral or policy research where relevant, regulatory practice and specialist counsel roles—not another master's by default.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build a strong regulatory-law publication and case-analysis record and enter law firms, corporate legal teams, regulators, financial institutions, policy organisations or specialist research centres.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish a niche in securities regulation, competition law, corporate governance, fintech regulation, financial markets, insolvency or regulatory enforcement.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior regulatory counsel, general counsel, regulatory-policy lead, enforcement specialist, partner or academic-policy leadership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine legal expertise with financial technology, AI regulation, data governance, market-structure knowledge and cross-border regulatory analysis.

rows.text: Produce a structured analysis of one corporate-regulatory issue using primary legislation and rules
Analyse one SEBI regulation/circular and produce a 10-page legal memorandum
Write a merger/anti-competitive-practice case analysis using primary decisions
Map the regulatory framework for one financial product or institution
Complete a governance case study covering board duties, disclosures and compliance
Analyse an enforcement order and identify the legal reasoning, evidence and remedy
Produce two policy briefs translating technical regulation into executive recommendations
Maintain CV, publications and a portfolio containing at least 4 substantial regulatory-law outputs

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

Not applicable to this Ph.D.-level starting point. If a four-year UG honours route is being considered separately, the additional year should be used for a substantial legal-research dissertation and stronger preparation for postgraduate/professional study.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Regulatory counsel should increasingly understand technology, data, AI, digital markets and financial infrastructure alongside traditional legal doctrine. The differentiator is the ability to translate changing rules into practical decisions for boards, institutions and regulators.

blocks.text: A research appointment and a practising-law position are different pathways. Foreign legal practice can require local qualification or admission in addition to immigration permission. Verify the destination jurisdiction's rules before treating a research position as a route to legal practice.
Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Regulatory Researcher / Regulatory Counsel → Senior Regulatory Counsel → Regulatory Lead / Specialist Counsel → Head of Regulatory Affairs / Partner → General Counsel / Regulatory Policy Director → Senior Regulatory Adviser
Typical progression can be approximately 0–3 years → 3–7 years → 7–12 years → 12–18+ years, depending on whether the career develops in private practice, industry, government or academia.

The senior profile should move beyond knowing individual regulations toward understanding how regulatory systems operate. Strong senior counsel will connect legislation, enforcement, market structure, technology, corporate governance and economic incentives, while being able to advise boards and institutions on practical regulatory consequences.
